The movement of men's hearts
is made so by [external] things.
They are touched off by things and move, thus they shape in [human] sound (sheng). Sounds respond to each and thus give birth to change. Change forms a pattern
thus they shape in [human] sound (sheng).
Sounds respond to each other
and thus give birth to change.
Change forms a pattern
The music is brought close and found enjoyable.,
and reaches the point of shields and axes, feathers and pennants,
and this is called Music (yue).
1.2 Music (yue) is that which arises from music (yin). 61
Its root
lies in the touching off of mens' hearts by [external] things.
for he whose heart is touched off to happiness,
his sound is spacious and leisurely
for he whose heart is touched off to joy,
his sound is expansive and far- reaching;

for he whose heart is touched off to anger, his sound is coarse and unyielding; for he whose heart is touched off to reverence, his sound is straightforward and upright; for he whose heart is touched off to love, his sound is harmonious and gentle. These six are not [inner] nature -- they are set in motion only after being touched off by things.62 For this reason, the former kings were cautious in what was used to touch them off (the people). Thus Ritual (li 4) was used to direct their wills,
Music (yue) was used to harmonize their voices (sheng),
Administration (zheng) was used to unify their actions,
and Punishment (xing JfIJ) was used to prevent their violations.
Ritual, Music, Punishment, and Administration --
their ends are one:
they are that which is used to unify the people's hearts and put forth the Way of Governance.
All music (yin) arises in the hearts of men.
Emotion is stirred within
and thus takes shape in sound (sheng).
Sound forms patterns,
and this is called music (yin).
For this reason,
the music of a [well-] governed age is peaceful,
so as to express happiness in the harmony of the administration.
The music of a chaotic age is resentful,
so as to express anger over the perverseness of the administration.
The music of a lost state is mournful,
so as to express thoughtfulness over the hardships of the people.
The Way of sound and music

connects with administration.64 [Zheng Xuan says: "This talks of how whether or not the eight timbres (yin) are in harmony depends upon the administration [of the state]. The 'Yu Zao' [chapter of the Li Ji] says: 'The blind musician in attendance judged whether the music were too high or low."'65]
1.4 Gong is the ruler,
shang is the minister,
jue is the people,
zhi is the affairs,
and yu is the things [of production].
If these five are not chaotic,
then there will be no discordant music (yin).
If the gong [tone] is chaotic, then [the music] is disorganized,
[indicating that] the ruler is arrogant.
If the shang [tone] is chaotic,
If the jue [tone] is chaotic, then [the music] is depressed,
[indicating that] the people are resentful.
If the zhi [tone] is chaotic, then [the music] is mournful,
[indicating that] the affairs are overburdening.
If the yu [tone] is chaotic, then [the music] is precipitous,
[indicating that] the wealth [of the state] is depleted.
If these five are all chaotic,
and transgress upon each other in turn,
this is called "man" (dissolute) [music].
If it is like this,

then the extermination and passing away of the state will occur in no time at all. [Zheng Xuan says: "'The five' refer to the ruler, minister, people, affairs, and things. In all cases of tones (sheng), the lower (zhuo W, literally 'murky') ones are revered and the higher (qing q清, literally 'clear') ones are lowly.68 Zhanchi Mt M. is the appearance of being broken down (bibai, 敝敗) and unharmonious. If the ways of the ruler, minister, people, or things are chaotic, then their [corresponding] tones (yin) will be chaotic in response. Huang 荒 is like san 散 (scattered). Bi RI is qing 傾 (inclined, slanted). The [Shang] Shu says, "Wang... mao huang... 王耄荒）69 The Yi Jing says: "Wu ping bu bi (無平不陂), "there is no leveling that will not slant").70]
1.5 The music of Zheng and Wei
is the music of a chaotic age.
It borders on dissoluteness (man 漫).
The music from among the mulberries atop the Pu River
is the music of a lost state.
The administration was disorganized
and the people dispersed.

Superiors were slandered and private ends were carried out, and it could not be stopped. [Zheng Xuan says: "Bi t is like tong i- (to be the same as). [Among] the lands above the River Pu there was a Sangjian -- it is from these waters that the music of a lost country came out. In ancient times, Zhou of the Yin Dynasty made Shi Yan compose some licentious music. After a short while, he drowned himself in the River Pu. Later, Shi Juan passed by there, and at night heard [the music] and wrote it down. He played it for Duke Ping of Jin. This is the story it refers to. Sangjian is south of Puyang. Wu ~ means wang M (to accuse unjustly)."]
1.6 All music (yin)
arises in the hearts of men.
Music (yue)
is that which connects with [ethical] human relationships and principles (lunli).
For this reason,
those who know sounds (sheng) but do not know music (yin) --
these are the birds and the beasts.
Those who know music (yin) yet do not know Music (yue) --
these are the common masses.
Only the superior man (junzi) can know Music (yue).
For this reason,
sounds (sheng) are investigated to know music (yin),
music is investigated to know Music (yue),
Music is investigated to know administration,
and the Way of Governance is complete.
For this reason,
those who do not know sounds (sheng) can not be spoken with about music (yin);
those who do not know music can not be spoken with about Music (yue).
To know Music (yue)
is to be close to Ritual (li).
If Ritual and Music are both attained to (de 4),
this is called "having virtue (de ,)."
"Virtue" (de 4,), means "attainment" (de 4).
For this reason,
the prospering of Music (yue) [at the sacrifice]
is not [a matter of] reaching the extreme in music (yin);
the Ritual of the communal ancestral sacrifice
is not [a matter of] extending to the utmost in flavors.
The se in the Temple to King Wen (qingmiao)
had red [-boiled] strings and sparse holes [in the bottom],
and with one singing and three sighing,
there would be left-over music.
In the Ritual of the Great Ancestral Sacrifice,
water (lit. "black wine") was held highest
and raw fish was put on the offering stands;
the great thick-soup was not mixed [with spices, etc.], and there would be left-over flavors.
For this reason, the making of Ritual and Music by the former kings
was not in order to exhaust the desires of the mouth, the belly, the ears, and the eyes. I
t was used in order to instruct the people to level-out their likes and dislikes

and to return to the proper center of the Way of mankind.74 [Zheng Xuan says: "Lun IA is like lei M (classification). Li f means fen $} (divisions). The birds and beasts know only that this is sound; they do not know the changes of its gong and the shang [tones]. When the eight timbres sound at once and are able to be in harmony, we speak of yue. Ji R means jin ir (close). If the achievements and failures of the administration are known, then the ritual order of the ruler, ministers, people, affairs, and things can be rectified. Long 9 means sheng ! (prosperous). Ji
1.7 Man is born and is still --
this is Heaven's nature (xing).
[He is] touched off by [external] things and [only then] moves --
this is [his] nature's desires.
Things arrive and the [faculty of] knowledge apprehends [them] --
only then do likes and dislikes take shape therein.
If likes and dislikes have no regulation within
and the [faculty of] knowledge is enticed from without,
[man] can not return to [reflect upon] himself,
and the principles of Heaven (tianli R ) are destroyed.
Now if the touching off of man by things is without limit
and the likes and dislikes of man have no regulation,
then this is [a matter of] things arriving and men being transformed [by] things.
For man to be transformed [by] things
is to destroy the principles of Heaven and to extend human desires to the limit.
At that point there are rebellious and false hearts,
and there are licentious and havoc-wreaking affairs.
For this reason,
the many do violence to the few,
the powerful intimidate the weak,
the intelligent cheat the stupid,
and the courageous cause suffering to the cowardly.
Ailments and sicknesses are not convalesced, x
and the elderly, young, orphaned, and childless can not obtain their place.

This is the way of great chaos.80 [Zheng Xuan says: (After ".. . this is nature's desires") "This talks of how the nature does not have desires if it does not perceive things." (After "... only then do likes and dislikes take shape therein") "Zhi - means lai R (to come). Zhi zhi h] 0 means that whenever each thing comes, then there is further knowing. (That is, the reduplication of the character gives the sense of repeated action). This talks of how when things are many, then the desires are more numerous. Xing JfI is like xian A (to appear)." (After "... the principles of Heaven are destroyed") "Jie j is fadu I (codes and standards). Zhi 0 is like yu 4Z (desires). You A is like dao 2, yin I (to lead, attract). Gong - is like ji E (the self). Li f is like xing i (nature)." (After ".... extend human desires to the limit") "Qiong ren yu NR A.. says that there is nothing that is not carried out."]
1.8 For this reason, the constructing of Ritual and Music by the former kings
[was a matter of] making regulation for the people.
The coarse hemp of mourning garments, crying and weeping --
these are what was used to regulate the mourning rites.
Bells and drums, shields and axes --
these are what was used to harmonize peace and happiness.
Marriages, caps and hairpins --
these are what was used to distinguish males and females.
Archery contests and celebrations, banquet entertainments --
these are what was used to engage in proper social intercourse.
Ritual regulates the people's hearts;
Music harmonizes the people's voices.
Administration is used to carry them out;
Punishment is used to prevent [transgressions against] them.
If the four

2. 樂論 The Discours of Music" 2.1 Music (yue) serves to unite (tong,
F[); Ritual cserves differentiate (yi, W).
With uniting there is mutual closeness;
differentiation there is mutual respect.
When Music gains the hand there is reckless abandon (liu L).
When Ritual gains the hand there is estrangement (li 0).
To unite (he -1) the emotions and to polish external appearances --
these are the affairs of and Music.
If the deportment of Ritual is established,
then the noble and the plebeian are separated into classes.
When the patterns of Music are uniform,
then those in high position and those in low position get along in harmony.
If likes and dislikes are made clear,
then the worthy and the unworthy are distinguished.
If punishments are used to prevent violence
and titles are used to esteem the worthy,
then the administration is on level ground.
Humanity (ren --) is used in loving them (the people)
and propriety (yi 4) is used in rectifying them --
if it is like this,

then the governance of the people will be implemented. [Zheng Xuan says: "Tong [ refers to harmonizing likes and dislikes. Yi qrefers to distinguishing between the worth and the lowly. Liu 'L refers to combined action without respect. Li irefers to living separately without harmony. [Of Ritual and Music] It is desired that they both be carried out, in a manner complete in both external refinement and internal qualities (binbinran M *i ,). Deng V are [social] classes.]
2.2 Music comes out from within,
Ritual comes into being from without.
Music comes out from within, thus it is still.
Ritual comes into being from without, thus it is ordered.
Great Music must be marked by ease,
Great Ritual must be marked by simplicity.90
If Music reaches the ultimate, there are no grievances.
If Ritual reaches the ultimate, [the people] do not struggle [with one another].
The governance of all under Heaven through deference
is what is meant by Ritual and Music.
Rebellious people do not arise,
the feudal lords submit like guests,
weaponry and armour are not employed,
and the five punishments are not made use of.
The masses are without suffering,
and the Son of Heaven is not angry. --
If it is like this,
then Music has reached its goal.
Uniting the affections of father and son,
making manifest the order of the old and the young,
so as to gain respect for the Son of Heaven throughout the land --
if it is like this,

then Ritual has been carried out. [Zheng Xuan says: "Harmony resides with the heart. Respect resides on the exterior. Wen :Z is like dong Mb (movement). Yi i (easy, peaceful) and jian f (simple), as with the qingmiao (odes to King Wen) and the Great Ancestral Sacrifice. Zhi - is like da i (to reach), xing I:T (to travel, be carried out). Bin - means xie S (to be in harmony, be united), Shi At means yong PJ (to use)"
2.3 Great Music shares in the harmony of Heaven and Earth.
Great Ritual shares in the regulation of Heaven and Earth.
There is harmony, thus the "hundred things" do not suffer loss;
there is regulation, thus [there are] sacrifices to Heaven and to Earth.
In the bright [sphere] there are Ritual and Music;

in the dark [sphere] there are ghosts and spirits. [After ". . . ghosts and spirits] "[Ghosts and spirits] are those that help Heaven and Earth in the maturation of things." The Yi Jing says: 'For this reason it is known that the nature and form of the ghosts and spirits are similar to Heaven and Earth.'94 The 'Wudi de' [chapter of the Da Dai Li Ji], in talking of the virtue of Huang Di, says: 'When he died, it was for a hundred years that the people held his spirit in awe.'95 The [Zuo] Commentary to the Chun Qiu says: '.. . the hosts of the Ruo'ao clan ...'96 This being so, the essential energy (jingqi S A) of the sages is called "shen" ( , "spirits"), and the essential energy of the worthy and the wise is called "gui" (1, "ghosts"). ]
In this way, then,
throughout the land [the people]
are combined in respect and united in love.
Ritual is that which combines respect through different affairs.
Music is that which unites love through different patterns.
The natures (qing) of Ritual and Music are united,

thus enlightened kings follow each other in them. Zheng Xuan: After "... followed each other by means of them"] "Yan e'I is to follow [precedents]. Confucius said: 'The Yin Dynasty followed the ritual of the Xia: wherein it took from or added to it may be known. The Zhou Dynasty has followed the ritual of the Yin: wherein it took from or added to it may be known.'97 Yan is sometimes written as 0 (yuan)."

Thus affairs go along with the times, Zheng Xuan: [After ". .. affairs go along with the times"] "This means that the performance of actions rest with their times. The "Li Qi" [chapter of the Li Ji] says: 'Yao conferred [the throne] upon Shun; Shun conferred [the throne] upon Yu. Tang deposed of Jie, and King Wen conquered Zhou. -- These were [a matter of it being the right] time.'98"

and names go together with accomplishments. [Zheng Xuan says: [After "Music ... Ritual ... shares in the ... of Heaven and Earth"] "This talks of going along with the energy (qi) and numbers (shu It, i.e. cyclic regularities, etc.) of Heaven and Earth." [Shi ) refers to] "[the hundred things] not losing their natures." [After "make sacrifices to Heaven and Earth"] "In the maturing of things (i.e. ripening of grains) [Heaven and Earth] perform a meritorious service, for which [the people] repay them." [After "In the bright ... Ritual and Music"] "[Ritual and Music are] those that teach men." [After ". . . ghosts and spirits] "[Ghosts and spirits] are those that help Heaven and Earth in the maturation of things." The Yi Jing says: 'For this reason it is known that the nature and form of the ghosts and spirits are similar to Heaven and Earth.'94 The 'Wudi de' [chapter of the Da Dai Li Ji], in talking of the virtue of Huang Di, says: 'When he died, it was for a hundred years that the people held his spirit in awe.'95 The [Zuo] Commentary to the Chun Qiu says: '.. . the hosts of the Ruo'ao clan ...'96 This being so, the essential energy (jingqi S A) of the sages is called "shen" ( , "spirits"), and the essential energy of the worthy and the wise is called "gui" (1, "ghosts"). ]
2.4 Thus bells and drums, flutes and chimestones,
feathers and pipes, shields and axes --
these are the instruments of Music.
Bowing and extending, lowering and raising heads,
positions and boundaries, slowness and quickness --
these are the patterns of Music.
Square and round grain vessels, offering stands and food vessels,
codes and standards, patterns and colors --
these are the instruments of Ritual.
Ascending and descending, raising and lowering,
the making of rounds, the removal and putting on of upper garments --
these are the patterns of Ritual.
Thus those who know the nature (qing) of Ritual and Music can create;
those who recognize the patterns of Ritual and Music can transmit.
Creators are called sagely;
transmiters are called enlightened.
Being enlightened or sagely
refers to transmiting or creating.
2.5 Music
is the harmony of Heaven and Earth.
Ritual
is the order of Heaven and Earth.
Harmony, thus the hundred things all transform;
order, thus the myriad things are all differentiated.
Music is created from Heaven,
Ritual is constructed through Earth.
If there is excess in the construction [of Ritual], there is chaos.
If there is excess in the creation [of Music], there is revolt.
Only after having a clear understanding of Heaven and Earth

can [the ruler] give rise to Ritual and Music. [Zheng Xuan says: "Hua it is like sheng I (to arise, be born). Bie 1IJ refers to their forms and bodies being different." [On "Music ... from Heaven, Ritual ... Earth"] "This talks of modeling after Heaven and Earth." "Guo A is like wu A (to error). Bao * is losing the meaning of the civil and military (wenwu iC A).]
2.6 The balanced exposition of [different] types without [mutual] injury
is the nature (qing) of Music.
Joy, happiness, and love
are the affairs of Music.
To stick to the proper center without inclinations
Solemnity, reverence, and obedience
are the institutions of Ritual.
Now as to Ritual and Music being employed in metal and stone,
surpassing [mere] sounds and music,
being used in the ancestral temples and at the altars to the spirits of the land and grain,
and being made to serve the mountains, rivers, ghosts, and spirits --
this is what [the ruler] shares in common with the people.
is the substance of Ritual.
For those whose accomplishments are great, their Music is complete;
and when their rule is established, construct Ritual.
3. "Yue Li" -- "Music and Ritual" 3.1 The kings, when their accomplishments are realized, Music,
for those whose rule is [established] everywhere, their Ritual is complete.
Dances of shields and axes are not complete Music.
Sacrificing with well-boiled [foods] is not [fully-] attained Ritual.
The five emperors in their different times
The three kings in their different eras
did not follow each other in Music.
did not cloak themselves in each other's Ritual.
When Music reaches the extreme, there is sorrow.
When Ritual is coarse, there is bias.
As to the deepening of Music and having no sorrow,
and Ritual's being complete and without bias,

is this [not] only [the work of] a great sage? [Zheng Xuan says: "The realization of accomplishments and the establishment of rule are simply [done] at the same time. Accomplishments are chiefly the achievements of kings; rule involves mainly the teaching of the people. The "Mingtang wei" [chapter of the Li Ji], talking of the Duke of Zhou, says, 'ruling the kingdom for six years, he brought the feudal lords together in attendance at the Hall of Enlightened Rule (mingtang), and constructed Ritual and created Music.100 Bian M is bian n 6 (to be everywhere). Music is made complete through [both] order (wen) and virtue (de), such as [is the case with] Xianchi A It.101 Confucius said, . Shao exhausts beauty, and it also exhausts goodness. Wu Aexhausts beauty, but it does not exhaust goodness.'102 Da i is ju (complete). [The] "Jiao tesheng" [chapter of the Li Ji] says: 'In the Suburban Sacrifice, it is blood; in the Great Ancestral Sacrifice it is raw [fish], in the three offerings [of wine] it is over-cooked and in the single offering it is well-cooked. In expressing reverence, one does not enjoy the flavors, but holds the scent of its vapors in highest esteem.'103 [Not following each other in Music or Ritual] talks of how there were deletions and additions." "Music is what people like. Its harm lies in transgression and exaggeration. Ritual is what people put effort into. Its harm lies in causing hardship and separation. Dun R means hou T1 (thick, deep, sincere)."]
3.2 With Heaven high and Earth low,
and the 10,000 things scattered and variegated,
the institution of Ritual is carried out.
Flowing without rest,
and uniting together in transformation,
Music arises therein. In spring it is born,
and in summer it grows --
this is humanity (ren).
In autumn it is harvested, and in winter it is stored --
this is propriety (yi).
Humanity is close to Music;
propriety is close to Ritual.
Music promotes harmony,
abides by the spirits, and follows Heaven.
Ritual distinguishes what is appropriate,
resides with the ghosts, and follows Earth.
Thus sages created Music to respond to Heaven,
and constructed Ritual to match the Earth.
When Ritual and Music are illuminated and complete,

then Heaven and Earth have obtained to [the world of] affairs. [Zheng Xuan says: "Ritual is differentiation, Music is uniting." (On the idea of Music and Ritual corresponding to the humanity and propriety of the four seasons) "This talks of Music modelling after yang and giving birth, and Ritual modelling after yin and yielding maturation." "Dunhe R1 1 means that in Music, unity is esteemed. Shuai $ means xun
3.3 Heaven is honorable and Earth is lowly;
and [the relationship of] the ruler and ministers has [thereby] been fixed.
When the low and the high have been set forth,
the noble and the plebeian have been put in place.
Movement and stillness have constancy,
and the small and the large have been differentiated.
The animals are grouped together by species,
and the plants are divided into classes,
thus their natures and life-spans are not the same.
In Heaven, representations (xiang W) are formed;
on Earth, shapes are formed --
in this way, then,
is Ritual the differentiation of Heaven and Earth.
3.4 Earth's energy (qi 9) rises up,
and Heaven's energy descends.
Yin and yang rub against each other,
and Heaven and Earth shake each other.
[The 10,000 things] are drummed up with thunder and lightning,
aroused forth with wind and rain,
set in motion by the four seasons,
warmed by the sun and the moon,
and the hundred transformations (hua it) arise therein.
In this way, then,

is Music the harmony of Heaven and Earth.108 [Zheng Xuan says: "Qi W is read as ji 52. Ji means sheng t (to ascend). Mo 9 means po I (to press upon). Dang A' is like dong b (to move). Fen E means xun ~ (to rush forth). Baihua - 4 means the hundred things are brought into life."]
3.5 If the transformations (hua) are not timely, then they do not give birth.
If male and female are not distinguished, then chaos arises.

This is the nature (qing) of Heaven and Earth. [Zheng Xuan says: "Bian t is bie VIJ (to separate, distinguish). Sheng "t is cheng -i (to form). If music suffers loss, then it harms things; if ritual suffers loss, then it makes men chaotic."]
3.6 Now as for Music and Ritual -- they extend to the limits of Heaven and lie low upon the ground;
travel through yin and yang and communicate with ghosts and spirits;

exhaust the heights, reach the farthest limits, and delve into the deep and thick. [Zheng Xuan says: "Ji means zhi - (to reach). Pan 4 is like wei . (to entrust, follow). 'High and far' means the three heavenly bodies sun, moon, and stars). 'Deep and thick' means the mountains and rivers. This talks of how, in the way of music and ritual, as above they reach Heaven and below entrust themselves to Earth, that between them there is nowhere they do not go."]
3.7 Music dwells in the great beginning,
and Ritual resides in matured things.109
That which manifests non-rest is Heaven,
and that which manifests non-motion is Earth.
That which has one in motion and one still
is [that which resides] among Heaven and Earth.

Thus the sages speak of "Ritual and Music." [Zheng Xuan says: "Zhu 91 refers to residing in (chu A). Da shi ; means the 'primal host' (shizhu ~ ~ 1) of the 'hundred things.' 4. "Yue Shi" -- "The Bestowal of Music" 4.1 In ancient times,
Shun made a five-string qin in order song the "Poem to the Southern Wind."112
Kui (Shun's master) was the first to construct Music with which to reward feudal lords.
4.2 Thus the making of Music by the Son of Heaven
is in order to reward those among the feudal lords who have virtue.
Only after their virtue is capacious and their teachings revered,
and the five grains ripen in accordance with the seasons,
are they rewarded with Music.
Thus for those who overwork the people in their rule,
the distance between the rows of their dancers is far;113
for those who allow the people relaxation in their rule,
the distance between the rows of their dancers is short.
4.3 Thus by observing their dance,
one knows of their virtue;
[just as] by hearing their posthumous titles,
one knows of their actions.
4.4 "Da Zhang" ("Great Manifestation" -- Yao's composition) means [Yao's virtue] is manifested;
"Xian Chi" ("[Virtue] is conferred upon all" -- Huang Di's composition, revised by Yao)
means all is completed;
"Shao" ("To Continue [the rule after Yao]" -- Shun's composition)
means to carry out [the rule];
"Xia" (Yu's composition)
means to make great (i.e. to expand the virtue of Yao and Shun);
and the Music of the Yin and the Zhou (i.e. Tang's "Da Huo" --"The Great Relief," and King Wu's "Tai Wu" -- "The Great Conquest")
exhausted [the scope of human affairs.
4.5 In the Way of Heaven and Earth,
if cold and heat are not timely, there is sickness,
and if wind and rain are not regular in their occurrence, there is hunger.
Teachings
are the cold and heat of the people --
if teachings are not timely, then harm is done to the age.
Affairs
are the wind and rain of the people --
if affairs are not regular in their occurrence, then there is no accomplishment.
This being the case, the making of Music by former kings
was in order to provide a model for governance.
If it is good, then the actions [of the people] strive to resemble the virtue [of the ruler].
4.6 Now to raise hogs and make wine
is not for the purpose of causing misfortune.
Yet when there is a great proliferation of jail terms and lawsuits,
it is that an indulgence in wine has given rise to misfortune.
For this reason, the former kings then made the wine ritual
a ritual wherein [only] a single offering [of wine] is given [at a time].
Guest and host [may] pay a hundred obeisances
and drink wine the whole day, yet do not get drunk therein.
This is what the former kings used to prepare against disasters caused by wine
Thus wine and food are what is used to unite men in enjoyment.
Music is what is used to [cause the people] to strive to resemble the virtue [of the ruler].
Ritual is what is used to put a stop to transgressions.
For this reason, when the former kings experienced a great loss (death),
they invariably had ritual by which to mourn it.
When they experienced a great blessing,
they invariably had ritual by which to enjoy it.
The division between mourning and enjoyment
all ends in Ritual.
Music --
it is what sages delight in,
and it can be used to make better the hearts of the people.
Its effect on people is deep;
it can alter habits and change customs.
Thus the former kings made manifest their teachings therein.

yet do not have any constancy happiness, joy, and anger.
They arise in motion in response being touched off by [external] things,
and only then do (shu) of the heart take shape therein.

5.2 For this reason,
[in the making of Music] the former kings based it on the emotions and natures (qingxing) [of man],
investigated it [and brought it into accord with] standards and numbers,115
and constructed it after the meaning of Ritual.
[In Music] they made it accord with the harmony of the [dual] breaths of life,
and be a pathway for the movement of the five constancies.116
It was made to [exhibit] the power of yang, yet not be scattered,
and the nature of yin, yet not be constricted;
[so that its] inflexible energy (gangqi J R) would not [give rise to] anger,
and its pliant energy (rouqi R Z ) would not [result in] timidity.
[These] four penetrations (sichang e 9 f) interact within [Music?]
and blossom forth without.
All (tones and other musical parameters?) are content in their positions and do not rob from each other.117
Only then is it (Music) established in the ranks of learning,
broadened in the regulation of its performance,
and is given reflection as to its patterns and colorings,
so as to put a measure on its virtue and good will.
The balance of small and large is put into the pitches [of the bells in the temples],
and the order [of the five tones] is aligned from beginning to end,
in order to represent the affairs and actions [of society].
The principles (li) of the close and distant, the noble and plebeian, the old and young, and male and female
are all made to take shape and appear in Music (yue).
Thus it is said:
"To observe Music -- is it not deep!"
5.3 If the land is worn out, the grasses and trees will not grow.
If the water is rapid, the fish and turtles will not be big.
If the breath of life (qi) is weakened, then living things will not come about.
If the age is chaotic, then Ritual is deceitful and Music is licentious.
For this reason, its sounds (sheng) are mournful yet not solemn,
happy yet not at peace,
slow and lax so as to violate its rhythm,
and drunk in indulgence so as to forget its roots.118
If it is broad, then it allows for debauchery;
if it is narrow,119 then [it causes one to] think of desires.
It excites a wild and unrestrained energy,120
and wipes out even and harmonious virtue.
Because of this, the superior man thinks little of it.
